dimensions.explanation: The stated actors are distributors. Promotion to a client covers both specific products and particular product types, including certain fund types and fund houses. The selected application remains within the circular’s SFC-authorised-fund context.

Neither gift nor discount is exhaustively defined. Additional returns and incentives may be gifts; that classification is not automatic. Actual fund return and distributor top-up return are expressly distinguished.

The parenthetical exception attaches to discounts of fees or charges. A separately identifiable discount does not expressly exempt another benefit in a combined offer. Whether a fee-linked rebate actually qualifies as a discount remains unresolved.

The selected standard says should not offer. The proposed compliance predicate models conformity to that stated standard without converting it into the separate statutory offence. May be considered preserves judgment over classification.

The restriction concerns offering gifts during promotion. No effective date, transition period or payment deadline is supplied. The FAQ’s 30 September 2010 date identifies a source, not a commencement date.

The gift control is independently relevant even when an arrangement is not a structured product. The Code and supporting FAQ are identified but not supplied in full; section 103 authorisation or exemption does not establish satisfaction of the gift control.

readings.distinction: The discount exception applies to the identified benefit, while product-type promotion remains covered. For example, an offer promoting funds of one fund house could combine a fee reduction with a separately identifiable shopping voucher. Assuming the voucher is a gift and not a fee discount, the fee reduction satisfies this control and the voucher fails it. The text does not support exempting the entire package because one component is a discount, or excluding it because no individual fund is singled out. A fee-linked cash rebate presents a genuine unresolved classification question: if it is a discount it satisfies this control; if it is a non-discount gift it fails. The packet does not supply enough criteria to choose between those classifications.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For the selected control, Paragraph 3.11 gift restriction for one offered benefit, true means that the in-scope benefit is either not a gift or qualifies for the fee-or-charge discount exception. False means that it is an in-scope gift outside that exception and fails the stated should-not-offer standard. This is a proposed interpretation of that control only; it does not determine compliance of other offer components, section 103 compliance or whole-firm compliance.
